target.title: fix(hooks): bound HOOK.md reads during hook install validation
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`resolveHookNameFromDir` in `src/hooks/install.ts` reads `HOOK.md` with an unbounded `fs.promises.readFile` call. A malicious or malformed hook package containing a multi-gigabyte `HOOK.md` could force the install path to buffer the entire file into memory just to extract the hook name from frontmatter, leading to OOM.

## Why This Change Was Made

`HOOK.md` is only parsed for a short frontmatter block (name, description). A 1 MiB cap is generous headroom for legitimate hook documentation while preventing the install path from being used as a memory exhaustion vector.

## User Impact

Installing a hook package with an oversized `HOOK.md` now fails fast with a clear size-limit error instead of risking process OOM.

## Evidence

- Added a regression test that writes a `1 MiB + 1` byte `HOOK.md` and asserts `installHooksFromPath` rejects with `File exceeds 1048576 bytes`.
- Local focused run: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/hooks/install.test.ts --run` passes (29/29 tests).


## Real behavior proof

I created a local hook directory with a `1 MiB + 1` byte `HOOK.md` and ran the regression test that exercises `installHooksFromPath`. The install path rejects the oversized file before parsing frontmatter:

```text
$ OPENCLAW_VITEST_MAX_WORKERS=1 node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/hooks/install.test.ts --run
[test] starting test/vitest/vitest.hooks.config.ts
 RUN  v4.1.9
 ✓ |hooks| src/hooks/install.test.ts (29 tests) 2510ms
     ✓ rejects an oversized HOOK.md to prevent OOM during frontmatter parsing
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  29 passed (29)
[test] passed 1 Vitest shard in 15.11s
```

The oversized `HOOK.md` test fails with `File exceeds 1048576 bytes`, confirming the bounded read is enforced before frontmatter parsing and no downstream install steps run.
